import Mathlib

namespace FieldShift

theorem shift_divisible_of_residue_support
    (E : Set ℤ) (h r c k : ℤ)
    (hne : E.Nonempty)
    (hperiod : h ∣ r)
    (hresidue : ∀ x ∈ E, h ∣ x - c)
    (htranslate : ∀ x ∈ E, ∃ y ∈ E, r ∣ x + k - y) :
    h ∣ k := by
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hne
  obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := htranslate x hx
  have hwrap : h ∣ x + k - y := dvd_trans hperiod hxy
  have hsum : h ∣ (x + k - y) + (y - c) - (x - c) :=
    dvd_sub (dvd_add hwrap (hresidue y hy)) (hresidue x hx)
  have heq : (x + k - y) + (y - c) - (x - c) = k := by ring
  rwa [heq] at hsum

theorem progression_residue
    (h t r t0 j q : ℤ) (ht : h ∣ t) (hr : h ∣ r) :
    h ∣ (t0 + j * t - q * r) - t0 := by
  have hmultiple : h ∣ j * t - q * r :=
    dvd_sub (dvd_mul_of_dvd_right ht j) (dvd_mul_of_dvd_right hr q)
  have heq : (t0 + j * t - q * r) - t0 = j * t - q * r := by ring
  rwa [heq]

theorem progression_no_wrap
    (b t j : ℤ) (ht : 0 < t) (hj0 : 0 ≤ j) (hjb : j < b) :
    0 ≤ j * t ∧ j * t < b * t := by
  exact ⟨mul_nonneg hj0 ht.le, mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hjb ht⟩

theorem progression_mod_representative
    (b t j : ℤ) (ht : 0 < t) (hj0 : 0 ≤ j) (hjb : j < b) :
    (j * t) % (b * t) = j * t := by
  exact Int.emod_eq_of_lt (progression_no_wrap b t j ht hj0 hjb).1
    (progression_no_wrap b t j ht hj0 hjb).2

theorem progression_distinct_mod
    (b t i j : ℤ) (ht : t ≠ 0)
    (hi : i ∈ Set.Ico 0 b) (hj : j ∈ Set.Ico 0 b) :
    Int.ModEq (b * t) (i * t) (j * t) ↔ i = j := by
  constructor
  · intro hmod
    have hindices := Int.ModEq.mul_right_cancel' ht hmod
    change i % b = j % b at hindices
    simpa only [Int.emod_eq_of_lt hi.1 hi.2, Int.emod_eq_of_lt hj.1 hj.2] using hindices
  · rintro rfl
    exact Int.ModEq.rfl

theorem odd_doubling_modEq_iff
    (b : ℕ) (hb : Odd b) (i j : ℕ) :
    Nat.ModEq b (2 * i) (2 * j) ↔ Nat.ModEq b i j := by
  constructor
  · intro hmod
    exact hmod.cancel_left_of_coprime hb.coprime_two_right
  · intro hmod
    exact hmod.mul_left 2

theorem odd_doubling_distinct_mod
    (b : ℕ) (hb : Odd b) (i j : ℕ) (hi : i < b) (hj : j < b) :
    Nat.ModEq b (2 * i) (2 * j) ↔ i = j := by
  rw [odd_doubling_modEq_iff b hb i j]
  exact ⟨fun hmod => hmod.eq_of_lt_of_lt hi hj, fun h => h ▸ Nat.ModEq.rfl⟩

theorem synchronized_differences_add
    (h a a1 s : ℤ) (hfirst : h ∣ a1 - a) (hsecond : h ∣ s - a1) :
    h ∣ s - a := by
  have hsum : h ∣ (a1 - a) + (s - a1) := dvd_add hfirst hsecond
  have heq : (a1 - a) + (s - a1) = s - a := by ring
  rwa [heq] at hsum

theorem commuting_pair_integer_normal_form
    {G : Type*} [Group G] (g d : G) (hcommute : Commute g d)
    {x : G} (hx : x ∈ Subgroup.closure ({g, d} : Set G)) :
    ∃ m n : ℤ, g ^ m * d ^ n = x := by
  induction hx using Subgroup.closure_induction with
  | mem x hx =>
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl
    · exact ⟨1, 0, by simp⟩
    · exact ⟨0, 1, by simp⟩
  | one => exact ⟨0, 0, by simp⟩
  | mul x y hx hy ihx ihy =>
    obtain ⟨m, n, rfl⟩ := ihx
    obtain ⟨p, q, rfl⟩ := ihy
    refine ⟨m + p, n + q, ?_⟩
    rw [zpow_add, zpow_add]
    exact (hcommute.zpow_zpow p n).mul_mul_mul_comm (g ^ m) (d ^ q)
  | inv x hx ih =>
    obtain ⟨m, n, rfl⟩ := ih
    refine ⟨-m, -n, ?_⟩
    simpa only [zpow_neg, mul_inv_rev] using (hcommute.zpow_zpow m n).inv_inv.eq

theorem commuting_pair_card_le
    {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (g d : G) (hcommute : Commute g d) :
    Nat.card (Subgroup.closure ({g, d} : Set G)) ≤ orderOf g * orderOf d := by
  let H := Subgroup.closure ({g, d} : Set G)
  have hg : g ∈ H := Subgroup.subset_closure (by simp)
  have hd : d ∈ H := Subgroup.subset_closure (by simp)
  have hgz : Subgroup.zpowers g ≤ H := by
    rw [Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure]
    exact (Subgroup.closure_le H).mpr (Set.singleton_subset_iff.mpr hg)
  have hdz : Subgroup.zpowers d ≤ H := by
    rw [Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure]
    exact (Subgroup.closure_le H).mpr (Set.singleton_subset_iff.mpr hd)
  let f : Subgroup.zpowers g × Subgroup.zpowers d → H :=
    fun p => ⟨p.1.1 * p.2.1, H.mul_mem (hgz p.1.2) (hdz p.2.2)⟩
  have hsurjective : Function.Surjective f := by
    intro x
    obtain ⟨m, n, heq⟩ := commuting_pair_integer_normal_form g d hcommute x.property
    refine ⟨(⟨g ^ m, Subgroup.zpow_mem_zpowers g m⟩,
      ⟨d ^ n, Subgroup.zpow_mem_zpowers d n⟩), ?_⟩
    exact Subtype.ext heq
  calc
    Nat.card H ≤ Nat.card (Subgroup.zpowers g × Subgroup.zpowers d) :=
      Nat.card_le_card_of_surjective f hsurjective
    _ = orderOf g * orderOf d := by
      rw [Nat.card_prod, Nat.card_zpowers, Nat.card_zpowers]

theorem closure_pair_eq_zpowers_of_power
    {G : Type*} [Group G] (g d : G) (v : ℕ) (hpower : g ^ v = d) :
    Subgroup.closure ({g, d} : Set G) = Subgroup.zpowers g := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · refine (Subgroup.closure_le _).mpr ?_
    intro x hx
    simp only [Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hx
    rcases hx with hx | hx
    · rw [hx]
      exact Subgroup.mem_zpowers g
    · rw [hx, ← hpower]
      exact Subgroup.npow_mem_zpowers g v
  · rw [Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure]
    apply Subgroup.closure_mono
    exact Set.singleton_subset_iff.mpr (by simp)

theorem field_diagram_group_card_bound
    {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G] (g d : G) (v : ℕ)
    (hcommute : Commute g d) (hd : d ^ 2 = 1) (hv : 0 < v)
    (hpower : g ^ v = 1 ∨ g ^ v = d) :
    Nat.card (Subgroup.closure ({g, d} : Set G)) ≤ 2 * v := by
  rcases hpower with hpower | hpower
  · calc
      Nat.card (Subgroup.closure ({g, d} : Set G)) ≤ orderOf g * orderOf d :=
        commuting_pair_card_le g d hcommute
      _ ≤ v * 2 :=
        Nat.mul_le_mul (orderOf_le_of_pow_eq_one hv hpower)
          (orderOf_le_of_pow_eq_one (by decide : 0 < 2) hd)
      _ = 2 * v := Nat.mul_comm v 2
  · have hdouble : g ^ (2 * v) = 1 := by
      calc
        g ^ (2 * v) = (g ^ v) ^ 2 := by rw [← pow_mul, Nat.mul_comm]
        _ = 1 := by rw [hpower, hd]
    rw [closure_pair_eq_zpowers_of_power g d v hpower]
    rw [Nat.card_zpowers]
    exact orderOf_le_of_pow_eq_one (by omega : 0 < 2 * v) hdouble

end FieldShift

# Statement fidelity: field-shift synchronization combinatorial core

This file documents `Main.lean` for claim `C_FIELD_COMBINATORIAL` in context
`CTX_FIELD_SHIFT`. Every declaration is in namespace `FieldShift`.

## Exact scope

This is the **combinatorial core only**. It is not a Lean formalization of finite
Chevalley-group restriction theory, actual edge module constructions, arbitrary
normalizer realizability, or any manuscript main theorem. Separate
representation-theoretic proofs supplied by the parent audit must justify
applying these arithmetic and abstract finite-group results to actual retained
edges and normalizers. No such application is an assumption or a conclusion of
this Lean source. No novelty or independent review is asserted.

## Arithmetic declarations

* `shift_divisible_of_residue_support`: for every set `E` of integers and all
  integers `h,r,c,k`, if `E` is nonempty, `h` divides `r`, every `x` in `E`
  satisfies `h | x-c`, and for every `x` in `E` there exists `y` in `E` with
  `r | x+k-y`, then `h | k`. This includes arbitrary wraparound representatives,
  arbitrary periods (including zero and negative periods), and arbitrary
  integer shifts. Finiteness of `E` and positivity of `h` are not needed.
  Translation containment suffices; equality of translated supports is stronger.
* `progression_residue`: if `h | t` and `h | r`, then every integer position
  `t0+j*t-q*r` differs from `t0` by a multiple of `h`, for all integers `j,q`.
* `progression_no_wrap`: if `t>0` and `0<=j<b`, then
  `0<=j*t<b*t`. The index hypotheses already force `b>0`.
* `progression_mod_representative`: under those same hypotheses,
  `(j*t) % (b*t) = j*t`. Thus these selected progression positions do not wrap
  before reduction modulo the full period.
* `progression_distinct_mod`: for all integers `b,t,i,j`, if `t` is nonzero and
  `0<=i,j<b`, then `i*t` and `j*t` are congruent modulo `b*t` if and only if
  `i=j`. In particular this covers all positive integer `b,t`. Together with
  the preceding two declarations, this is the support noncollision/no-carry
  statement: assigning one digit to each selected position never assigns two
  digits to the same position. It does not assert a representation-theoretic
  tensor-factor decomposition or a theorem about arbitrary overlapping sums.
* `odd_doubling_modEq_iff`: for every odd natural `b` and all natural `i,j`,
  congruence of `2*i` and `2*j` modulo `b` is equivalent to congruence of `i`
  and `j` modulo `b`. This is a universal cancellation statement, not an
  enumeration of tested moduli.
* `odd_doubling_distinct_mod`: consequently, for all `i,j<b`, congruence of
  their doubled indices modulo odd `b` is equivalent to `i=j`. This includes
  `b=1` and supplies the odd unitary doubling noncollision property.
* `synchronized_differences_add`: for all integers `h,a,a1,s`, the hypotheses
  `h | a1-a` and `h | s-a1` imply `h | s-a`. Identifying one common
  intermediate exponent in the actual representations is outside this source.

## Abstract group declarations and the proved normal form

* `commuting_pair_integer_normal_form`: in any group, if `g,d` commute, every
  element of `Subgroup.closure {g,d}` is `g^m*d^n` for some integers `m,n`.
  This existence is **proved by subgroup-closure induction**, including the
  product and inverse cases. It is not an input hypothesis.
* `commuting_pair_card_le`: in any finite group, commuting `g,d` generate a
  subgroup of cardinality at most `orderOf g * orderOf d`. The proved integer
  normal form supplies a surjection from the product of their cyclic subgroups.
  Mathlib's kernel-checked cyclic-subgroup cardinality theorem then counts
  those subgroups. No bounded normal form is assumed.
* `closure_pair_eq_zpowers_of_power`: in any group, `g^v=d` implies that
  `Subgroup.closure {g,d}` is exactly the cyclic subgroup generated by `g`.
* `field_diagram_group_card_bound`: for every finite group `G`, all `g,d` in
  `G`, and every positive natural `v`, if `g,d` commute, `d^2=1`, and
  `g^v=1` or `g^v=d`, then
  `Nat.card (Subgroup.closure {g,d}) <= 2*v`. In the first branch the preceding
  surjection is counted using `orderOf g<=v` and `orderOf d<=2`. In the second
  branch the subgroup is cyclic and `g^(2*v)=1`. Neither commutativity of the
  ambient group nor faithfulness of an action is required.

The source imports the prebuilt Mathlib workspace for Lean 4.31.0 and adds no
axioms, proof holes, unsafe computation, or external decision procedures.
Standard Lean/Mathlib logical foundations are the only background assumptions.
